findings.evidence: `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/AEMeasurable.lean:352: theorem AEMeasurable.indicator (hfm : AEMeasurable f μ) {s} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : AEMeasurable (s.indicator f) μ`; `Set.indicator_self_add_compl` is already used at Marcinkiewicz.lean:329. Every use of `hcongr` in the file is the single `apply hcongr` at line 331.
findings.fix: Take the cut *set* from the representative but the *summands* from `v`: `S := {x | ENNReal.ofReal (c*t) < ‖hv.mk v x‖ₑ}` (measurable), `g₁ := S.indicator v`, `g₂ := Sᶜ.indicator v`. Then `g₁ + g₂ = v` on the nose by `Set.indicator_self_add_compl`, so `hadd g₁ g₂ (hv.indicator hSmeas)` already gives `T v ≤ᵐ[ν] T g₁ + T g₂`; `‖g₂ x‖ₑ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c*t)` holds a.e. (enough, since `hinfty` sees only `eLpNormEssSup g₂ μ`), and `hint` still goes through via `Measure.restrict_congr_set`. Drop `hcongr` from both signatures and the corresponding argument at MaximalFunction.lean:462.
findings.issue: `hcongr : ∀ {g h}, g =ᵐ[μ] h → T g =ᵐ[ν] T h` is an avoidable hypothesis on `T`, present in both `mul_measure_ofReal_lt_operator_le_setLIntegral` (line 307) and `lintegral_rpow_operator_le` (line 405). It is needed only because the split is built from `g := hv.mk v` rather than from `v`, so `T v` has to be transported to `T (g₁ + g₂)` (line 330).

findings.evidence: `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/BorelSpace/Metric.lean:215-227`: `variable {ε} [MeasurableSpace ε] [TopologicalSpace ε] [ContinuousENorm ε] [OpensMeasurableSpace ε] ... protected lemma Measurable.enorm`. Mathlib states the analogous Lp results the same way (`Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:909,965`). `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/BorelSpace/Basic.lean:183: instance (priority := 100) BorelSpace.opensMeasurable`.
findings.fix: Replace `[BorelSpace G]` by `[OpensMeasurableSpace G]` in the `Operator` section variable block. `BorelSpace.opensMeasurable` is an instance, so the `G = ℝ≥0∞` specialization in MaximalFunction.lean is unaffected.
findings.issue: `[BorelSpace G]` is stronger than the proof uses and stronger than Mathlib convention. The only measurability facts about `G` are `hgmeas.enorm` (line 325) and `hv.enorm` (line 415), i.e. `Measurable.enorm` / `AEMeasurable.enorm`, which are stated for `[OpensMeasurableSpace ε]`.

summary: The operator-level theorems carry two assumptions stronger than needed: an a.e.-congruence law on `T` that the proof can avoid entirely by splitting `v` itself rather than its measurable representative, and `[BorelSpace G]` where only `[OpensMeasurableSpace G]` is used. Otherwise the split into distributional engine plus operator wrapper, and the removal of the maximal-function-specific truncation duplicate, is at the right level.
